title: Brotli2Shell: Frequently asked questions for Google Brotli decoder vulnerability (CVE-2026-111497)
date_basis: Publisher date and named author.
summary: Maps Brotli2Shell, Node2Shell, HTTP2Shell and Broccoli2Shell to one CVE and surveys downstream exposure and release paths.
limitations: Cross-product synthesis, not independent discovery or reproduction of every affected product. Its 26 October statement that the CVE was not in KEV is superseded by CISA's 27 October addition. Linked third-party exploitation claims retain their original uncertainty.

verification.basis: Publisher date, byline, alias mapping, dependency distinctions and dated exploitation/KEV qualifications inspected; current catalog status checked separately against official JSON.

title: RCE via OOM corruption
date_basis: Maintainer advisory published_at verified through GitHub API.
summary: Maintainer-confirmed PHP memory-corruption issue associated with out-of-memory handling and unauthenticated remote code execution under affected conditions.
limitations: Affected versions and demonstrated paths do not count vulnerable websites or successful compromises. Advisory inspected, exploit not reproduced.

verification.basis: Maintainer description, version ranges, credits and stable identifiers inspected; publication metadata crosschecked through GitHub API.

title: RCE via stale global state
date_basis: Maintainer advisory published_at verified through GitHub API.
summary: Documents stale request-owned state surviving fatal-error cleanup and subsequent unsafe reuse, with configuration-dependent memory disclosure, corruption or code execution.
limitations: Not a universal exploitability claim. Separate variants and configuration requirements matter; later PHP notices must also be consulted. Exploit not reproduced.

verification.basis: Maintainer advisory identity, description and affected/fixed branches inspected; CVE and published_at verified through GitHub API.

title: Today's PHP Security Release, and How We're Strengthening PHP Security
date_basis: Publisher date and corporate byline.
summary: Traces signs of the OOM issue to 2024, subsequent AI-assisted exploit demonstrations, resource and decision bottlenecks, fixes and disrupted disclosure.
limitations: Participant account, not an independent incident investigation. Claims about other parties' disclosure conduct remain attributed; no causal attribution of attacks to a particular leak is established.

verification.basis: Dated maintainer account, historical discovery, reporting timeline, staffing and disclosure sections inspected. Embedded social-media responses are not adopted as evidence.

title: How the PHP Security Team Handles Your Reports
date_basis: Publisher date and named byline.
summary: Describes human reproduction and classification of security reports, welcoming validated AI-assisted submissions while reporting 15 published CVEs and 106 closed non-vulnerability, duplicate or non-reproducing reports since July.
limitations: The 106 are not an AI false-positive count or rate: submissions have mixed origins and outcomes. Not a measured workload comparison with a no-AI counterfactual.

verification.basis: Byline, date, report counts, classification discussion and AI-report guidance inspected; no access to the private submission queue.

title: PHP2Shell: A tale of two PHP remote vulnerabilities
date_basis: Dated entry in Calif's research index; write-up credits Ryan Austin. August discovery dates are not publication dates.
summary: Describes human-directed AI-assisted variant analysis informed by PHP vulnerability history, leading to reproducible exploit paths and coordinated reporting.
limitations: Researcher account without a controlled human-only comparison. Initial discovery used generally available models; human expertise and target selection remain material. Technical claims not independently reproduced here.

verification.basis: Research index date, explicit writing credit, discovery history, method and application/SAPI distinctions inspected. No exploit code executed or downloaded.

title: PHP2Shell: AI uncovers critical RCE vulnerabilities affecting 70% of the Internet
date_basis: Publisher author list and date.
summary: Reports AI-assisted discovery, adaptation and lab demonstrations of PHP exploit chains across representative applications, with a responsible-disclosure timeline.
limitations: Title overgeneralizes prevalence as affected share. Selected demonstrations are not an internet-wide compromise census. Research-effort comparisons are retrospective estimates, not randomized evidence; commercial and model-provider interests apply.

verification.basis: Author/date, impact table, AI-method discussion, disclosed model involvement and timeline inspected. Marketing sections and uninspected demonstrations not treated as independently verified outcomes.

title: Amazon Threat Intelligence identifies PHP2Shell exploitation prior to public disclosure in MadPot
date_basis: Publisher date and CJ Moses byline.
summary: Reports a PHP2Shell exploitation attempt in MadPot telemetry on 17 October, before public disclosure, while leaving real-world success and the actor's information source unresolved.
limitations: Attempt is not confirmed compromise. Anonymized infrastructure does not establish attribution, a leak source or AI use by an attacker. No representative attack-success denominator.

verification.basis: Dated threat-intelligence report, attempt timestamps and explicit uncertainty about successful exploitation inspected; raw sensor data not audited.

title: Obstacles to Weaponizing PHP2Shell Likely Constrain Immediate Widespread Exploitation
date_basis: Publisher date and author block.
summary: Separates crash demonstrations, laboratory RCE and reliable exploitation across deployments; reports no successful wild exploitation observed in its scope as of 23 October.
limitations: Dated sensor-limited negative observation, not proof of no exploitation globally. Later KEV entries supersede a present-tense no-exploitation claim, without invalidating the earlier observation.

verification.basis: Date, authors, laboratory-versus-wild distinction, configuration barriers and assessment inspected. Technical reproductions not repeated.

title: PHP2Shell: Exploitation Attempts and Remediation Trends
date_basis: Publisher time element and bylines inspected in Chrome.
summary: Reports unsuccessful chains in its own telemetry, acknowledges stronger public honeypot RCE evidence elsewhere, and describes declining observed exposure without attributing the decline solely to patches.
limitations: Own telemetry is not global absence. Changing coverage, network restriction and retirement affect exposure trends. Public honeypot success under favorable conditions does not establish universal reliability.

verification.basis: Full article, authors, date, exposure definitions, unsuccessful-attempt analysis and acknowledgement of external RCE evidence read in Chrome. No exploit kit executed.

title: Censys PHP2Shell Exposure Tracker
date_basis: Dated observation of evolving dashboard, not a claimed first-publication date.
summary: Provides version-inferred service exposure and observed transitions to fixed versions, with explicit qualifications about hidden versions, backports, scan lag and counting units.
limitations: Services are not unique websites, machines or organizations. Reported versions are not exploitability tests. Detection changes and hidden versions limit inference; observed upgrades lag actual deployment.

verification.basis: Loaded dashboard timestamp, service counts and complete notes/limitations inspected in Chrome; stale search-index counts not used as current data.

title: Usage statistics of PHP for websites
date_basis: Observation date for a daily-updated statistics page, not its launch date.

limitations: Prevalence is neither vulnerable-version exposure nor compromise. Detection and sampling matter; the reported share is not all websites without qualification.

verification.basis: Chrome inspected the exact denominator wording and 69.2 percent daily snapshot. Full survey methodology not independently audited.

verification.basis: Executive summary, default behavior, mitigations, selected fixed releases and rebuild/redeployment guidance inspected; exhaustive package table not independently tested.

date_basis: Publisher calendar date and named authors.

verification.basis: Maintainer article, authors, date, counts, reproduction requirements and fuzzing comparison inspected. Restricted individual bug reports not reviewed.

date_basis: Publisher calendar date and named author.

verification.basis: Full short article, date, author, release-linked count, optimistic interpretation and human-comprehensibility footnote inspected.

title: Measuring LLMs' impact on N-day exploits
date_basis: Publisher publication date and author list.

limitations: Developer-run selected-task evaluation with prepared artifacts, large token budgets, retries and some safeguards disabled. Standalone engine and local privilege escalation are not complete remote intrusion campaigns. Best-trial times and API charges are not representative operational costs; no independent replication performed here.

verification.basis: Date/authors, Firefox and Windows setups, graders, budgets, trial aggregation and reported outcomes inspected. Artifacts and graders not rerun.

title: Patch the Planet: global response coordination as agents uncover critical vulnerabilities
date_basis: Publisher date and corporate authorship.

verification.basis: Date, attribution of discovery/fixing, proposed coordination stages and qualified defender-window statement inspected. New services and funding not independently evaluated.

title: Who is Responsible for Tackling Professional Deskilling?
date_basis: Publisher Published Online date: 23 September 2026; accepted 10 September, received 1 June.

Its characterization of Lee et al. as critical-thinking decay exceeds what that self-report survey establishes. Clinical, aviation and programming outcomes are not interchangeable; mitigation effectiveness needs evaluation.

verification.basis: Full open-access publisher HTML, author, DOI, publication history, sections 1-5, references and disclosures inspected in local Chrome after automated 405 failures. Lee et al. primary abstract checked separately; remaining cited studies not all independently appraised.

date_basis: Publisher-displayed publication date and author biography.

limitations: Selected prices and practitioner experience, not a causal market study. Token-volume shares are not dollar shares. Future prices, switching costs and supplier margins cannot be inferred from provider counts or current rate cards. Not every historical announcement was independently checked.

verification.basis: Full blog article including pricing timeline and speculative explanations inspected. Selected price fields cross-checked against official Anthropic and OpenAI announcements; Vercel's linked methodology inspected separately.

title: A Mathematician Reads the AI Future
date_basis: Local Chrome publisher heading, Steven Strogatz byline and timestamp: 25 October 2026, 8 AM ET.
summary: Strogatz distinguishes obtaining mathematical results from understanding them and from the human experience of discovery. Alongside anxiety about research careers and training, he describes Townsend's constructive program of AI-assisted problem solving, question selection, theory building and interpretation. Reported reactions illustrate contested purposes of mathematical work, not a consensus or a measured learning effect.
limitations: Expert essay with selected first-person accounts, not a representative survey, causal study or proof verification. Numerical breakthrough announcements and reported problem solutions are not independently validated by reading this essay. Cornell events and correspondence remain attributed reporting; the pure/applied distinction is an interpretive simplification, not an established taxonomy of attitudes. Concerns about training and careers are not measured long-run outcomes. A user-supplied Safari printout enabled full-text reading; the publisher page may remain subscription-restricted.

verification.basis: Complete essay read in a user-supplied 10-page Safari PDF printout, including ending and author biography. Printed title, Steven Strogatz byline, timestamp and canonical URL match the prior local Chrome identity inspection. Full-text appraisal does not independently verify mathematical proofs, numerical announcements or reported correspondence. Historical Chrome preview scope is preserved separately.
